result:
A component re-renders when its own state changes, its parent renders, or a context it reads changes, so nearly every surprise is one of those three firing more often than you think. Find out which with the React DevTools Profiler by enabling "Record why each component rendered".

The most common cause is a parent re-rendering, which re-renders all children regardless of props. Fix it by wrapping the child in `React.memo`, or better, by moving the changing state down into the component that actually uses it, or passing the expensive subtree as `children` so the parent's state change doesn't recreate it.

`React.memo` then fails silently if you pass props that get a new identity every render, such as inline objects, arrays and arrow functions (`style={{...}}`, `onClick={() => ...}`). Stabilise them with `useMemo` and `useCallback`, hoist constants outside the component, or pass primitives instead of objects. If you're on React 19 with the React Compiler, it does this memoisation for you.

Context re-renders every consumer whenever the provider's `value` changes identity, so `value={{ user, setUser }}` inline re-renders them all on every provider render. Memoise the value with `useMemo`, and split rarely changing and frequently changing data into separate contexts.

Store selectors (Redux, Zustand) cause the same problem when they return a fresh object or array each call. Select the smallest primitive you need, or pass a shallow equality function (`shallowEqual`, `useShallow`).

An effect that sets state derived from props or other state causes an extra render every time. Compute the value during render instead and delete the effect; an effect whose dependency is an unstable object will also loop for the same reason as above.

Unstable keys (`key={Math.random()}`, or an index on a reordered list) make it remount rather than just re-render, losing state. Use a stable id from the data.

Finally, if you see exactly double renders only in development, that's `StrictMode` deliberately double-invoking, and nothing needs fixing.
